subject: Demo — coordinating APAC slots and calendar date mismatch
messages:
From: Lina Koh <lina.koh@aquavista.co.sg>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@aquavista.co.sg
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 09:05:00 +0800
Subject: Quick demo request — availability this week (SGT times)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the follow-up. We’d love a product walkthrough for Redwood Optimize next week. Would any of the following work for your team?

- Option A: Fri Jul 24, 2026 — 09:00 AM SGT
- Option B: Fri Jul 24, 2026 — 03:30 PM SGT

We have folks joining from Tokyo and Sydney, so some teammates may see different calendar dates in their panes. I attached our availability PDF. Also note: when we pasted the draft invite into Outlook one attendee saw the date as Thu 23 — looks like the client calendar defaulted to PDT earlier and flipped the display. Can you confirm the final date/time and send an invite that includes TZs?

Attaching: avl_availability_week_30.pdf

Best,
Lina Koh
Head of Operations
AquaVista Labs

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Koh <lina.koh@aquavista.co.sg>
Cc: hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 11:22:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Quick demo request — availability this week (SGT times)

Hi Lina — thanks for sending availability and flagging the calendar mismatch. Copying Hiro and Vivek so we have APAC coverage.

Quick notes to avoid the cross-day confusion: SGT = UTC+8, JST = UTC+9, AEST (Sydney standard time) = UTC+10. In plain conversions:
- 09:00 AM SGT = 10:00 AM JST = 11:00 AM AEST
- 03:30 PM SGT = 04:30 PM JST = 05:30 PM AEST

If your attendees are in both Tokyo and Sydney, Option A (09:00 SGT / 11:00 AEST) is the cleaner morning window. We prefer to avoid running demos after 6:00 PM AEST for attendee fatigue.

To prevent the previous calendar flip, I will:
1) Send a fresh Google Calendar invite that lists all three local times in the event title and the body.
2) Include a short TTL note: “Event times shown in SGT/JST/AEST — double-check your calendar client settings (time zone & DST).”

Does Fri Jul 24 at 09:00 SGT work for you? If yes, I’ll send the invite and include a dial-in + recording consent.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

From: hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 14:01:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Quick demo request — availability this week (SGT times)

Stephanie — sounds good. One operational note from Tokyo: if any customer participant is joining from NSW (Sydney) and needs lunch overlap, 11:00 AEST is fine but we should avoid pushing later than 17:30 AEST. If they prefer a later Australian-friendly slot, we can offer 04:00 PM SGT / 05:00 PM JST / 06:00 PM AEST as a second choice, but that’s near the upper edge.

I can cover the demo if you want me on the call — happy to jump in for the segment on Optimize cost profiles.

-Hiro

From: Lina Koh <lina.koh@aquavista.co.sg>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@aquavista.co.sg
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 18:10:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Quick demo request — availability this week (SGT times)

Thanks — 09:00 AM SGT on Fri Jul 24 works for our group. Confirming that converts to 10:00 AM JST / 11:00 AM AEST in our clocks.

We did see the “Thu 23” issue in one invite; looks like one of our attendees had their calendar client set to US Pacific (PDT) and the DNS/locale mapping flipped the displayed date. Appreciate the all-TZ invite — that will avoid confusion.

Please send the calendar invite with the three local times in the title and include dial-in links. I attached a screenshot of the mis-rendered invite so you can see how it looked on Outlook.

Attachments: invite_screenshot.png

See you Fri — Lina
